response: {"text":"The paper tries to make sense of the way a common low‑carbon steel behaves when it is first deformed and later left to age, using the concept that the material’s tiny crystal grains and the zones where they meet control its properties. By applying this idea, the author shows how the initial yield stress changes with the size of the grains, offering a clear link between grain dimensions and the stress at which the metal begins to flow. The discussion also argues that the aging process involves two simultaneous actions: the repair of the thin layers that exist at the grain interfaces and a strengthening that occurs inside the grains themselves. Finally, possible characteristics of those interfacial layers are considered, suggesting they play a key role in both the early yielding and the later hardening."}
